rows.definition: The environment knob bounding the per-worker warm worktree pool: the maximum number of IDLE detached worktrees kept per LANE under the worktree root. Unset, unparsable or negative reads as the default; 0 disables the pool and reproduces the pre-pool create/reap behaviour byte for byte.
rows.distinction: Not a pool of in-memory objects like PagedKVPool (x2-pool-pagedkvpool) and not a pool of accounts like BuildSeatPool (x2-pool-buildseatpool): this bounds ON-DISK git worktrees, so its cap governs disk residency and cold-sweep reclamation rather than allocation. It is a cap on IDLE members only — a worktree held by live work is never counted against it.

rows.definition: The resolver that reads PoolCapEnv and returns the effective per-lane idle-worktree cap, failing open to the default on anything unreadable so a typo'd knob can never mean unbounded. Both Prepare and Reap consult it, so the pool is on or off for the whole lifecycle rather than per call site.
rows.distinction: Not the knob itself (x2-pool-workerworktreepoolcapenv): that is the env NAME, this is the parsed integer plus the fail-open policy applied to it. The distinction matters because the guarantee 'a bad value is never unbounded' lives here, not in the constant.
